To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the proteasome subunit composition of DC changes during maturation and that the proteasomes are replaced by immunoproteasome containing LMP2, MECL‐1, and LMP7.
DC up‐regulate proteasome subunit LMP2 and the PA28α/β complex during maturation and that the proteasome composition changes during maturation.
dendritic cells up‐ regulate immunoproteasome subunits and the proteasomal activator PA28 upon stimulation by CD40 ligand, lipopolysaccharide, and proinflammatory cytokine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the proteolytic system of antigen presentation, in particular the proteasome, and its functional implications for antigen processing and presentation.
the molecular basis of DC maturation, a key process in the immune system.
the regulation of the proteasome composition in human DC and the functional implications of the proteasomal changes for DC function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DC maturation is accompanied by the up‐regulation of immunoproteases and the neosynthesis and activation of the proteasome activator PA28.
the proteasome composition in DC is changed in a way that it can be considered to have a specific DC – proteasome.
the proteasome is an essential component of the DC machinery and that its composition changes during maturation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
proteasomes are a major factor determining the peptide repertoire of MHC class I molecules in DC.
DC are equipped with a proteasome system which allows them to generate peptides with high binding affinity to MHC class I molecules and to present them efficiently to CD8 T cells.
the composition of the proteasome changes from constitutively expressed to inducible proteolytic activity during maturation of DC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proteasome composition changes during DC maturation.

the proteasome composition of DC is tightly regulated and that DC are equipped with the machinery for the production of immunosubunit‐rich proteasomes and PA28, which may be relevant for the processing of antigens in the context of MHC class I and II molecules.
DCs up‐regulate the proteasomes and the immunoproteasome subunits in order to generate the peptides for the MHC I and MHC II molecules.
